---

## SEC Filing Analysis: North Haven Private Income Fund LLC — 8-K / March 25, 2026

---

### A. Relevance Verdict

**HIGHLY RELEVANT TO PRIVATE CREDIT**

This is a real-time monthly portfolio update from one of the largest non-traded private-credit BDCs in the U.S., filed just 14 days after the fund publicly capped investor redemptions at 5% — directly intersecting multiple live private-credit stress themes.

---

### B. One-Line Takeaway

Morgan Stanley's North Haven Private Income Fund — which recently returned only ~$169 million to investors after capping redemptions at 5% — now discloses a $7.48 billion portfolio with a 22% software concentration and only $13 million in new February commitments, signaling a defensive posture amid mounting industry stress.

---

### C. What's New

- **New unit issuance (March 1, 2026):** The fund sold approximately 1,505,645 Class S units at **$18.40/unit** for an aggregate offering price of **~$27.70 million**, with the final unit count determined on March 23, 2026. This is the freshest disclosed subscription price.
- **Dual distribution declared (March 23, 2026):** A regular distribution of **$0.1250/unit** plus a **special distribution of $0.0213/unit**, both payable ~April 6, 2026 to holders of record March 31, 2026. The special distribution is in addition to the regular dividend — not a replacement.
- **Current portfolio par value disclosed:** As of February 28, 2026, the fund's aggregate par value is **~$7,484.4 million** across 310 portfolio companies and 44 industries — a concrete current-month figure not previously in public filings.
- **Deployment sharply slowed:** New investment commitments in February 2026 were only **~$13.0 million**, 100% in private senior secured loans — an extremely modest figure relative to the fund's $7.5B scale.
- **Software sector concentration quantified:** Software is explicitly disclosed as the single largest industry exposure at **$1,646.6 million, or 22.0% of portfolio par value**.
- **New unit pricing benchmark:** The $18.40/unit purchase price as of the March 1, 2026 subscription date is the most current NAV-based pricing disclosed, against which any future markdown would be measured.

---

### D. Most Important Points

- **Portfolio scale:** 310 borrowers, 44 industries, ~$7,484.4 million aggregate par value as of February 28, 2026. The fund is among the largest non-traded BDCs in the U.S.
- **First-lien dominance:** 97.1% of investments are first-lien debt by par value; second lien is only 0.4%. This matters for recovery analysis if defaults rise.
- **Floating-rate exposure:** 99.9% of debt investments are at floating rates — a double-edged sword as rate sensitivity runs both ways for borrower stress.
- **Software is the single largest sector** at $1,646.6 million / 22.0%. Software exposure among private credit funds that do direct lending is an estimated 26% on average, according to Morgan Stanley — this fund is slightly below that average but still highly concentrated.
- **Deployment pace is very slow:** $13.0 million in new commitments in February across a $7.5B book equates to roughly 0.17% of NAV deployed in the month — consistent with a defensive posture or deal-flow drought.
- **New subscriptions of only ~$27.7 million:** For a fund of this scale, this is a modest capital raise, suggesting inflow momentum has slowed materially, consistent with the broader redemption story.
- **BSL exposure:** 5.9% of total investment commitments are in broadly syndicated loans, primarily for cash management — this is a potential liquidity buffer but also a mark-to-market exposure.
- **Current unit price $18.40:** This is the operative NAV per Class S unit — the benchmark against which any future markdowns or investor losses would be calculated.
- **Regular + special distributions maintained:** The fund is continuing to pay both a regular and a special distribution despite the redemption cap, signaling management's desire to project financial health.
- **Private senior secured loans: 94.1% of total commitments** — the filing confirms the portfolio remains defensively structured, but concentration in software complicates any blanket "senior secured is safe" narrative.

---

### E. Why It Matters Now

This filing lands at the epicenter of a live private-credit liquidity story. North Haven Private Income Fund LLC honored less than half of investors' redemption requests in Q1 and stuck to its quarterly 5% repurchase cap, with total redemption requests reaching 10.9% of shares outstanding, or roughly $169 million. That redemption cap was disclosed just 14 days ago. Now, this 8-K shows the fund issuing new units and disclosing a portfolio with **22% software exposure** — precisely the sector under the most scrutiny. Morgan Stanley itself recently warned default rates in private credit direct lending could surge to 8%, with pressure concentrated in sectors vulnerable to AI disruption, such as software. The fact that a Morgan Stanley-managed fund carries $1.65B in software loans, while Morgan Stanley simultaneously warns about software default risk, is a headline-ready tension. The deployment slowdown ($13M new in February) and muted subscriptions ($27.7M) further reinforce that the fund is managing defensively, not offensively expanding.

---

### F. Filing Details Extracted

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Filer** | North Haven Private Income Fund LLC |
| **Form type** | 8-K |
| **Filing date** | March 25, 2026 |
| **Period of report** | March 23, 2026 |
| **Company / fund / issuer** | North Haven Private Income Fund LLC (formerly Morgan Stanley Private Income Fund LLC); managed by MS Capital Partners Adviser Inc. (Morgan Stanley affiliate) |
| **Named lenders / agents / counterparties** | Not clearly disclosed in this filing |
| **Dollar amounts** | ~$27.70M new Class S unit subscription; $7,484.4M portfolio par value; $0.1250/unit regular distribution; $0.0213/unit special distribution; $13.0M new February investment commitments; Software exposure $1,646.6M |
| **Maturity dates** | Not clearly disclosed in this filing |
| **Interest-rate / spread terms** | 99.9% floating rate (underlying portfolio); no spread terms disclosed |
| **Key covenant or amendment terms** | Not clearly disclosed in this filing |
| **Sector** | Private senior secured direct lending, middle-market; software (22.0%), insurance services (9.4%), commercial services (7.7%), healthcare (6.4%), professional services (5.9%), IT services (5.5%) |
| **Watchlist entity match** | **Yes** — fund was subject to a redemption cap event (5% cap vs. 10.9% requested) disclosed March 11, 2026 |

---

### G. Signals Reporters Should Notice

- **Software at 22% of par ($1.65B):** AI-driven disruption is pressuring legacy software models, and software exposure is significant in many direct lending portfolios and may be understated by traditional industry classifications. North Haven's 22% allocation is a live stress-test target.
- **$13M of new February commitments on a $7.5B book:** This near-zero deployment rate is a signal the fund is not putting new capital to work — either by choice (defensive) or due to deal scarcity. Worth comparing to prior months.
- **Redemption cap + continued new unit issuances:** The fund is simultaneously capping outflows (5% quarterly redemption limit) and raising new money ($27.7M). This asymmetry — easier to get in than get out — warrants scrutiny of the fund's offering documents and investor disclosures.
- Industry-wide redemption requests spiked in late 2025 and early 2026, with several large non-traded BDCs and interval funds capping or slowing withdrawals. North Haven is part of this broader pattern — the filing should be read alongside peer fund disclosures.
- **Dual distribution while under redemption pressure:** Paying both a regular ($0.1250) and special ($0.0213) distribution in the same cycle that redemptions were capped is a potential investor-relations signal worth probing — is the fund using distributions to retain investors who might otherwise redeem?

---

### H. Routine vs. Non-Routine

**Routine / expected:**
- Monthly Reg FD portfolio update (standard for non-traded BDCs with ongoing subscriptions)
- Item 3.02 unregistered unit sale disclosure (standard for non-traded BDC monthly subscription closings)
- First-lien/floating-rate portfolio composition consistent with prior disclosures
- Distribution declarations consistent with prior quarterly cadence
- Broad industry diversification across 44 sectors

**Potentially non-routine / notable:**
- Filing comes 14 days after a high-profile redemption cap event; the new subscription price ($18.40) is the first NAV-linked number disclosed post-cap
- Software sector at 22.0% ($1.65B) is a material concentration into the sector most under scrutiny in the current market
- February new commitments of only $13.0M — unusually low for a fund of this size; this may reflect deliberate capital conservation
- New Class S subscriptions of $27.7M are modest relative to the fund's scale; inflow deceleration appears real
- Maintenance of special distribution simultaneous with redemption cap warrants follow-up — is the distribution policy being used as a retention tool?

---

### I. Questions for Follow-Up

1. **What was the monthly new commitment run rate in prior months (e.g., Q3–Q4 2025)?** A comparison would confirm whether the $13M February figure represents a sharp deceleration or is within normal range.
2. **What is the non-accrual rate and PIK loan percentage in the $1.65B software book?** The 8-K does not disclose credit-quality details — these would appear in the 10-Q/10-K.
3. **Has the fund's NAV per unit declined since subscription pricing was set?** The $18.40/unit price is described as an estimate; the quarter-end closing procedure may produce a different number.
4. **Are any of the software borrowers in the portfolio known stressed names (e.g., those trading below 80 cents in secondary markets)?** A PitchBook analysis noted a record $25 billion of speculative-rated software loans trading below 80 cents as of January 31.
5. **Why is the fund declaring a special distribution at the same time it capped redemptions?** Is this consistent with the fund's investment policy statement and the interests of remaining investors?
6. **What percentage of the $27.7M in new March subscriptions came from reinvested distributions vs. new investor capital?** This distinction matters for assessing real new inflows.
7. **Are the 5.9% broadly syndicated loans showing mark-to-market stress?** These are the fund's most liquid and most market-price-sensitive assets — and the most transparent signal of portfolio stress.
8. **Is Morgan Stanley's own research (warning of 8% default rates in software-heavy private credit) informing the fund's underwriting of its own software book?** The conflict between the parent's macro view and the fund's portfolio is a legitimate editorial angle.

---

### J. Evidence from the Filing

**Item 3.02 (Unregistered Sales):**
> "As of March 1, 2026, North Haven Private Income Fund LLC sold approximately 1,505,645 of the Company's Class S units for an aggregate offering price of approximately $27.70 million, reflecting a purchase price of $18.40 per unit."

**Item 7.01 — Distributions:**
> Regular distribution: $0.1250/unit; Special distribution: $0.0213/unit — both declared March 23, 2026, payable ~April 6, 2026 to record holders March 31, 2026.

**Item 7.01 — Portfolio composition (as of February 28, 2026):**
> 310 portfolio companies, 44 industries, aggregate par value ~$7,484.4 million; 97.1% first lien, 0.4% second lien, 2.5% other; 99.9% floating rate; 94.1% private senior secured; 5.9% broadly syndicated.

**Item 7.01 — New deployment:**
> February 1–28, 2026: New commitments of ~$13.0 million, 100% private senior secured loans.

**Item 7.01 — Industry table (top exposures):**
> Software $1,646.6M (22.0%); Insurance Services $699.5M (9.4%); Commercial Services & Supplies $577.2M (7.7%); Health Care Providers & Services $479.7M (6.4%); Professional Services $442.9M (5.9%); IT Services $411.8M (5.5%). [Table truncated in filing excerpt.]

---

### K. Final Newsroom Brief

**INTERNAL ALERT — March 25, 2026 | North Haven Private Income Fund LLC | 8-K**

North Haven Private Income Fund LLC, Morgan Stanley's ~$7.5 billion non-traded private-credit BDC, filed an 8-K today disclosing a March 1 subscription close of ~$27.7 million in new Class S units at $18.40/unit, alongside a February portfolio update showing 310 borrowers and $7.48 billion in aggregate par value. What is new and notable: the fund's software sector exposure stands at **$1.65 billion (22.0% of par)** — its single largest industry concentration — exactly as Morgan Stanley's own analysts warned that default rates in private credit direct lending could surge to 8%, with pressure concentrated in sectors vulnerable to AI disruption, such as software. This filing arrives just 14 days after North Haven publicly capped redemptions at 5% against 10.9% of requests, citing the need to avoid selling assets during periods of "market dislocation." The fund's February new investment commitments of only $13 million — near-zero relative to its $7.5B book — suggest defensive capital conservation, and new subscriptions of $27.7M indicate materially slowing inflows. The simultaneous maintenance of a regular plus special distribution while gating exits warrants close scrutiny. **Uncertainty:** The filing does not disclose non-accruals, individual borrower stress, or the quarter-end NAV closing figure — those will be material when the Q1 2026 10-Q is filed. **Suggested priority: Immediate** — connect to the March 11 redemption cap story and the software default risk narrative.
